data.long_meaning: Athya is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘Satya’, meaning truth. In Hindu mythology, Athya is the goddess of truth, honesty, and morality. She is the embodiment of divine truth and righteousness. The name Athya carries the meaning “Goddess of Truth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Athya usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of truth and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Another reference to 'Athya' is found in the Mahabharata, an epic Sanskrit poem of ancient India, where Athya is mentioned as a sage and as a teacher of yoga. He is also described as having lived during the time of the Pandavas, which is estimated to be around the 4th or 5th century BCE.
